questions.question: Describe the method for drawing the development of a rectangular box with a lid, including the conventions for fold lines, cut lines and glue flaps, and state how the net is checked.
questions.expected_answer: Draw the base to true length and width; attach the four sides to its four edges, each rising to the true height and as wide as the edge it attaches to; attach the lid to the top edge of one side, usually the back, at the base's size; add glue flaps as trapeziums slightly shorter than the edge on the free vertical edge of each pair of adjacent sides and a tuck flap on the lid. Fold lines are thin dashed or chain lines, cut lines thick continuous lines, and flaps are labelled. Check that there are six faces for a closed box, that no two faces fold onto the same position, that no position is left unfilled, and that every pair of edges that meet when folded are equal in length.

questions.question: For a loaded structure such as a swing or a bicycle, explain how to identify the force on a named part, and state where steel is placed in reinforced concrete and which steel section best resists bending with the least mass, with reasons.
questions.expected_answer: Ask what the load is trying to do to the part: a chain or cable is pulled and can only be in tension; a seat or crank arm loaded across its span bends; a spindle that is turned is in torsion; a post carrying weight is in compression and bends under wind; a bolt between plates pulled in opposite directions is in shear. In reinforced concrete the steel goes near the stretched face, at the bottom of a beam between supports and near the top over a column, with stirrups for shear and concrete cover to protect against rust and fire, because concrete is weak in tension and steel is strong in it. The I-beam resists bending with the least mass because its flanges lie far from the neutral axis where bending stress is greatest and its web carries the shear, so almost all its material works; depth matters more than width, which is why a ruler on edge is stiffer than one laid flat.

questions.question: Set out the four parts of a balanced examination answer on the impact of a material and write such an answer for plastic shopping bags.
questions.expected_answer: Name the material and its use; give at least one positive impact with a reason or example; give at least one negative impact with a reason, located at a life-cycle stage; and reach a judgement or propose a solution such as reduce, reuse, recycle, redesign, replace or regulate. Example: thin plastic shopping bags are waterproof, strong for their mass and almost free, so they made carrying goods easy for shoppers and traders; they are made from oil and at the disposal stage they blow into fences, rivers and drains where they persist for decades and harm animals; South Africa responded with a minimum thickness and a levy so bags are reused, and a further step is to replace them with durable reusable bags and improve collection and recycling.
